doc.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996

title: Milt Fillius and the Hamilton jazz weekend
summary: He recalls meeting Milt Fillius in Arizona, admires his support of jazz, and the college setting.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: How long have you known Milt?
Since I came to New York. I knew who he was because he was with Cab Calloway’s band. This was in the 40s.
No, I’m saying I wonder how long you knew Milt Fillius?

Oh, Milt Fillius. I met him out in Arizona I think at a jazz festival out in Arizona at the Paradise Valley Jazz Party. They have these wonderful parties Don Miller throws. They still go on, they’re wonderful. And Milt, well you know him because of the school, but he puts his money where his mouth is. He loves jazz to the point of you know supporting it. And he looks forward to these as much as we do. And I never, he’ll ask me, “How do you feel about --” this guy. And I have learned, with my funny colored hair, everybody plays good. Some people play better, but everybody plays good, you know anybody that gets to a certain level. And I’ll say, “Why do you want Joe Blow?” He says, “Well we’ve had him here” and so forth and so on. “Oh I couldn’t get this guy and I couldn’t get this guy but I could get him. I say, “He’s fine.” Don’t fight it. When he told me that Clark was going to do it, the first question I says was, “How is Clark,” you know, “How is he?” He says, “He’s fine, he’s going to be fine.” I had no idea he was this good. Because this is the Clark I remember and loved from the last picture. But Milt Fillius, I wish there were more Milt Filliuses.
To help keep the music happening. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -15-

Yeah, he believes in it. He puts his money where his mouth is. I like that. And it’s nice that this school, I mean I didn’t know about this school before I came up here the first time. And it’s like an MGM idea of what a college should look like, it really is. I mean I can see Peter Lawford and you know and Bonita Granville and all those people, you know in the costumes, the sweaters. Lana Turner as a teenager, I can see it here. And of course the weather this weekend has been incredible. I said, “Fillius, you must have friends in high places.”
He does. All places he has friends.
